mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent commercial registry in the foreign investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the origin jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state: notarize the certificate if required, obtain an Apostille from the origin jurisdiction's competent authority, then arrange notarized Chinese translation in China. If the origin jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state: notarize the certificate if required, obtain consular legalization from the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the origin jurisdiction, then arrange notarized Chinese translation in China. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Active Registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or tax authority in the foreign investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-Convention origin: local notarization (if required) plus Apostille by the origin competent authority, then notarized Chinese translation in China. Non-Apostille origin: local notarization (if required) plus consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the origin jurisdiction, then notarized Chinese translation in China. Use only one authentication path; never combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing WFOE incorporation, bank account opening and corporate seal procurement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor's board of directors or authorized corporate body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-Convention origin: execution before a notary, then Apostille from the origin competent authority, then notarized Chinese translation in China. Non-Apostille origin: execution before a notary, then consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the origin jurisdiction, then notarized Chinese translation in China. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative paths and must not be sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association, Charter or Memorandum and Articles of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor's corporate secretary, legal representative or competent registry (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-Convention origin: certified copy notarized locally and then apostilled by the origin competent authority, followed by notarized Chinese translation in China. Non-Apostille origin: certified copy notarized locally and then legalized by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the origin jurisdiction, followed by notarized Chinese translation in China. The two authentication systems are mutually exclusive and cannot be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Foreign Investor's Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-Convention origin: banker's signature notarized if required, then Apostille by the origin country's competent authority, then notarized Chinese translation in China. Non-Apostille origin: banker's signature notarized if required, then consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the origin jurisdiction, then notarized Chinese translation in China. Apostille and consular legalization are separate and parallel routes; never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register of Directors and Shareholders of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate service provider, company secretary or registry in the foreign investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-Convention origin: notarized certified copy plus Apostille from the origin competent authority, then notarized Chinese translation in China. Non-Apostille origin: notarized certified copy plus consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the origin jurisdiction, then notarized Chinese translation in China. Apostille and consular legalization cannot be combined sequentially; only one route applies based on the origin state's membership.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), authorized signatories and counterparties against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN sanctions lists, China's domestic sanctions and anti-money laundering blacklists (PBOC and Ministry of Public Security), EU and UK sanctions lists as secondary cross-references, and local court enforcement, bankruptcy and adverse-public-record databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person (PEP), family member or close associate of a PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or source of funds involving crypto, bearer shares or offshore shell vehicles. Screening must be completed before name reservation, before UBO filing, before bank account opening, and on a continuous risk-based basis, with independent third-party AML tools, identity and address verification, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, and adverse-media review. Any positive match or red flag must be escalated to the AML compliance committee and reported to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center (CAMLMAC) where required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and the SAMR Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform administered by the State Administration for Market Regulation and local Market Regulation Administrations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be in Chinese; an English name may be registered separately for banking and trade purposes but must correspond to the Chinese legal name. The Chinese name must follow the four-tier naming structure: administrative division plus distinctive name or transliterated foreign investor name plus industry or business feature plus organizational form (limited liability company/Co., Ltd.). Phonetic transliteration of a foreign investor's name into Chinese characters is permitted, and the English name cannot supersede the Chinese name. All contracts, bank accounts, customs records and tax filings reference the Chinese name and the Unified Social Credit Code.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If SAMR rejects a proposed name, the applicant receives a written rejection notice specifying the prohibited or sensitive token. The applicant must correct and submit a new name application through the same online portal, or, if the rejection is contested, file an internal review application with the issuing Market Regulation Administration within 15 business days. If the internal review is adverse, the applicant has 60 days to apply for administrative reconsideration before the next-higher SAMR or the relevant people's government. A judicial appeal may be filed with the competent People's Court within 6 months after the administrative reconsideration decision or, if no reconsideration is filed, within 6 months of the rejection notice. The name reservation may be extended only by re-filing before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office for a manufacturing WFOE. The local Market Regulation Administration requires a physical business site evidenced by a lease, property ownership certificate, or government-recognized incubator address; tax authorities require actual operational substance including employees, production or warehousing activity, and utility usage. For ISIC 2790 grid-tie solar inverter manufacturing, on-site production and storage premises are mandatory, and an unregistered mailbox or virtual address creates a material risk of license refusal, bank account rejection, and administrative penalties. Free-trade-zone incubator addresses may be acceptable only for non-manufacturing holding entities, not for a factory WFOE with statutory product certification requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 75-85% probability of an announced or unannounced physical inspection by the municipal SAMR and tax authority within the first 12 months after registration. Inspection checklist: registered address matches the business license; lease, property-rights certificate and landlord identity are available on-site; employees are physically present and social insurance registration is current; actual solar-inverter production or at least warehouse and office operations exist; electricity, water, payroll and logistics records support commercial substance; inventory, import/export documents and statutory licenses for grid-tie solar inverters are maintained; environmental protection and fire-safety inspection approvals are posted; and the publicized contact information is operational. Failure of any checklist item may trigger rectification orders, fines, mandatory deregistration and revocation of the foreign investment filing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Chapter II (incorporation and governance of limited liability companies), Articles 7, 10, 27, 32, 33, 47, 51, 59, 60 and 74; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 28 and 29; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (2022), Articles 8, 16 and 17; and the SAMR Enterprise Registration Administrative Provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Market Supervision Administration at the district/city level where the WFOE registered office is located; online through the Integrated Market Entity Registration Service Platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application, filed together with the articles of association, notarized/legalized foreign investor documents, identity certificates of the legal representative and statutory officers, and the registered office lease.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. There is no statutory minimum paid-up registered capital for a general WFOE limited liability company in China, but the subscribed capital must be reasonable for the proposed business scale and must be contributed in full within five years after establishment under the 2023 Company Law. The funds must be remitted to and recorded in the company's local bank account; a blocked escrow account is not required by the State Administration for Market Regulation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online compliance runs through the nationwide Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal with the STA's Golden Tax Phase IV system used for VAT invoice reconciliation and electronic fiscal clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporation: the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is incorporated under the Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), and the issued business license contains the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which operates as the mandatory taxpayer identification number for corporate income tax, VAT, and other consolidated taxes. 2) Tax registration completion: within the statutory period after the business license, the WFOE files tax registration information confirmation through the Electronic Tax Bureau portal, submitting legal representative identity, registered address, capital structure, business scope, bank account details, and accounting/fiscal system information to the competent STA office. 3) Taxpayer activation: the STA activates the entity's resident enterprise status and the applicable tax returns/filing obligations, including enterprise income tax, VAT, individual income tax withholding on employees, stamp duty, urban maintenance and construction tax, and education surcharges. 4) VAT status: the entity applies for general VAT taxpayer status (mandatory once annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000, or voluntarily if accounting records are complete) and receives a VAT invoice quota in the Golden Tax system. 5) E-invoice setup: the entity registers for the fully digital electronic invoice platform and, where required, configures the STA-approved electronic invoice data interface/API for ERP-based issuance. 6) Non-resident alternative: a foreign non-resident enterprise with China-source income and no permanent establishment must complete non-resident tax registration through the e-Tax portal or in-person with the competent authority, obtain a non-resident taxpayer identification number/certificate, and rely on payer withholding obligations; a WFOE is not a non-resident taxpayer for national tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity classification election for income tax. A WFOE limited liability company is compulsorily classified as a resident enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income. VAT status (general vs. small-scale taxpayer) is an administrative election/registration choice, not an entity classification election; BEPS Action 2-style hybrid outcomes are countered by the general anti-avoidance rule and controlled foreign corporation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Tax registration is automatic from the issuance of the business license; there is no minimum turnover threshold for registration. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000, while entities at or below that threshold may remain small-scale VAT taxpayers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-controlled electronic VAT invoice management system (Golden Tax Phase IV and the fully digital electronic invoice platform). Special VAT invoices carry unique encrypted invoice numbers and are uploaded in real time to the tax authority; issuance, red-letter reversal, purchase-side confirmation, and tax-rate validation are performed electronically. Anti-fraud controls include cryptographic signatures, automatic line-item transmission, statutory invoice serialization, and mandatory digital stamping/sealing; ERP/accounting system issuance is only valid when connected through the STA-approved official electronic invoice interface/API.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods export zero-rating applies only where the solar inverter/equipment is physically loaded and exported from China's customs territory; the exporter must be a general VAT taxpayer; the export must be evidenced by an electronic Export Goods Customs Declaration; the goods must not be prohibited or restricted from export; sales proceeds must be received from an overseas buyer in convertible foreign exchange and repatriated/settled within the statutory foreign-exchange window; and the exporter must file the export sale in the VAT 'exemption, credit, and refund' system to claim the 0% export rate and refund of residual input VAT. Qualifying cross-border services, including certain technology and after-sales digital services consumed entirely outside mainland China, may also be zero-rated when the overseas recipient, overseas consumption, service contract, and foreign-exchange receipt are documented.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Customs Declaration; the export-equivalent bill of entry)
Export sales contract or purchase order signed with the offshore buyer
Commercial invoice issued to the overseas buyer
Bill of Lading or air waybill (original/electronic negotiable transport document evidencing physical exit)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank/SAFE export-proceeds collection and settlement certificate
VAT invoice for the export sale as required in the export-rebate filing package
Export tax refund declaration form (exemption and refund/exemption-only) and the electronic data record transmitted through the STA-Customs export information system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective STA and China Customs cross-reconciliation. If any customs declaration, transport document, foreign-exchange receipt, or commercial trade document is false, incomplete, or uncorroborated, the claimed 0% rate is revoked, the 13% output VAT is assessed, late-payment surcharge is imposed at 0.05% per day, and administrative penalties of 50% to five times the tax evaded apply under the Tax Collection and Administration Law. Fraudulent export-rebate applications also trigger criminal liability under the Criminal Law for fraudulently obtaining export tax refunds, with fines and imprisonment up to life imprisonment in aggravated cases; tax authorities may additionally suspend or revoke the exporter's export-rebate filing qualification and general VAT taxpayer status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the delegated authority for foreign-exchange administration in China (Mainland)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange-rate regime for the RMB under a current-account convertible framework. Current-account items, including trade in goods, services, and operational profit remittances, are conditionally convertible: banks verify the genuineness of the underlying transaction through contracts, commercial invoices, customs declarations, and tax certificates. Capital-account items remain highly regulated. FDI equity injections, cross-border loans, and repatriation of invested capital require SAFE registration or approval and are subject to the Foreign Investment Access Negative List. There are no statutory surrender quotas for export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic accounts or sell it on the interbank market at market-determined rates. Profit remittance is practical but requires corporate income tax clearance, dividend withholding tax payment, audited financial statements, and the bank's compliance review. Because the solar-inverter business generates genuine trade flows and the WFOE has no statutory minimum registered capital, the treasury should maintain separate CNY and FCY accounts, register every cross-border capital movement with SAFE, and maintain a full audit trail to satisfy the 'real demand' standard for current-account convertibility, especially for trade settlement and profit distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory percentage surrender of export proceeds to the central bank. Under China's current-account total-volume monitoring framework, export goods proceeds must be repatriated to the exporting WFOE's domestic account through a designated licensed bank; the inward remittance must be matched against customs export declarations and should normally be collected within 90 days from the date of export declaration for general trade. The WFOE may choose to retain export receipts in a current-account foreign-exchange deposit account or convert them to CNY at market rates. Any overdue, unreconciled, or artificially inflated export proceeds will trigger SAFE administrative scrutiny, potentially lower the entity's trade facilitation classification, and require supplemental documentary evidence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary banking relationship in Mainland China. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Airwallex, Wise, MultiPass, and Currenxie are not licensed by PBOC or SAFE to open domestic RMB settlement accounts, issue Chinese corporate account numbers, or clear CNY through CIPS. They cannot legally replace a Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank for trade settlement, VAT/tax payment, payroll, or SAFE-mandated FX transaction filings. At most, an offshore EMI may be used by the parent or a Hong Kong treasury vehicle as a concentration wallet for non-CNH currency collections, but the WFOE must maintain its onshore treasury and all cross-border trade flows through a licensed Chinese bank. Any attempt to use an EMI as an orchestrating account for the PRC entity will be rejected at onboarding and will trigger AML red flags.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For opening a CNY basic deposit account, the statutory legal representative of the WFOE must normally appear in person at the bank branch with original passport, board resolutions, entity establishment documents, and corporate chops. The bank will conduct a face-to-face compliance interview and biometric verification. If the legal representative is an overseas resident, most Tier-1 state commercial banks will still require physical branch attendance; a notarized and consular-legalized power of attorney may be accepted in limited cases where the attorney appears in person and the compliance committee approves, but remote consular proxy opening is generally not available for an operating WFOE. The FDI capital account and foreign-currency current account will trigger an additional interview with the finance officer to explain business substance, source of funds, projected trade volumes, and the use of proceeds. These institutions strictly reject accounts with no physical presence or with an unverified legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-ownership chain with opaque Hong Kong and offshore intermediate holding companies preventing a clean beneficial-ownership map of ultimate non-resident shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial Ownership Registration Certificate or BO register from every relevant jurisdiction; legalized certificates of incorporation and current registered-agent letters for the entire holding chain; complete organizational chart with notarized passport copies and Chinese consular legalization for every material beneficial owner above the 25% threshold; audited shareholder registers; and source-of-wealth evidence including bank statements, personal net-worth statements, and tax returns for each ultimate owner to demonstrate clean formation and funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent product classification and end-use risk around solar inverter semiconductors, possible dual-use components, and export to sanction-sensitive buyers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ECCN and harmonized-system classification prepared with a licensed Chinese customs broker; detailed product technical datasheets and complete bill of materials; commodity jurisdiction review confirming no ITAR or dual-use classification; restricted-party screening results covering UN, EU, OFAC, and Chinese export-control lists for all counterparties and beneficial owners; customer end-user certificates for overseas buyers; and full trade-chain evidence comprising invoices, packing lists, and carrier documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI capital injection sourced from a parent with unclear liquidity, circular wiring, or private bridging-loan funding that raises source-of-funds concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE-issued FDI Foreign Exchange Business Registration and Information Confirmation Form; board resolutions from both the parent and the WFOE authorizing the registered capital injection; parent audited financial statements, bank statements, and cumulative cash-flow evidence; source-of-wealth documentation such as acquisition agreements, dividend declarations, or asset-sale contracts explaining the original USD/CNY funding; and a post-receipt capital verification report issued by a licensed PRC CPA firm confirming the paid-in registered capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early profit repatriation or material intra-group management fees paid against a low-substance WFOE, creating AML suspicion of transfer-pricing abuse, tax evasion, or base-eroding payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transfer-pricing documentation comprising functional analysis, economic-substance memorandum, inter-company agreements for royalties or management services, and benchmarked arm's-length profit-level indicators; audited PRC GAAP financial statements; corporate income tax clearance certificate and electronic tax payment receipts; board minutes authorizing any dividend distribution or fee payment; proof of withholding tax payment on dividends or service fees filed with the Chinese tax authority; and the SAFE FX purchase/payment application with the underlying service or trade contract attached.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the overseas parent's capital injection via a SWIFT MT103 wire to the WFOE's designated FDI capital account at a licensed Chinese bank. In Field 70, reference the SAFE FDI registration number and state 'FDI REGISTERED CAPITAL INJECTION'. Use the SAFE-designated Balance of Payments purpose code for inbound direct investment equity injection; the receiving bank will map this in its local BOP reporting system under the inward direct-investment capital category. The wire amount must match the amount recorded in the SAFE FDI information system; funds are posted to the capital account and cannot be released to the CNY operating account unless the negative-list compliance review passes. After receipt, complete a statutory capital verification with a licensed CPA firm if required, and record the contribution in the company's registry and accounting books. All subsequent conversion of capital funds into CNY must be for permitted operating expenses within the WFOE's actual business scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For genuine trade settlements, use standard SWIFT MT103 wires for operational payments and for payments evidenced by customs declarations and commercial contracts. For large procurements of solar inverter components, open commercial letters of credit using SWIFT MT700 issuance and MT707 amendment messages, with the beneficiary receiving payment against conforming shipping documents. Documentary collections (documents against payment and documents against acceptance) are acceptable for established counterparties and lower-risk periodic transactions, with the bank acting only as courier and remittance processor. All outbound current-account trade payments must be reported to SAFE with the appropriate BOP codes, matched against the WFOE's export/import customs data, and cleared through CIPS for RMB-denominated cross-border payments or SWIFT/CHIPS for USD and other convertible currencies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY forward contracts against USD and EUR for firm export/import commercial exposure, supported by genuine underlying invoices, contracts, or letters of credit and settled through a licensed Chinese bank.

Plain-vanilla CNY/USD and CNY/EUR foreign-exchange options, either calls or puts, with real trade exposure, no embedded leverage, and mandatory product-risk acknowledgement under derivative-suitability reviews.

Cross-currency interest-rate and principal swaps for long-term foreign-currency debt, external borrowing, or capital-repatriation exposure, registered with SAFE as derivative transactions under the external debt or capital framework.

Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards only for the overseas parent or Hong Kong treasury center to hedge non-mainland CNH positions; onshore WFOE instruments remain strictly deliverable because RMB is not a non-convertible currency within China.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report (integrated annual report under the Interim Regulations on Enterprise Information Publicity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, and local SAMR offices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 in the calendar year immediately following the fiscal year being reported; no general extension window is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing results in inclusion on the SAMR List of Enterprises with Abnormal Business Activities; if the omission is not remedied within three years, the enterprise is added to the List of Serious Violations and Untrustworthy Enterprises, triggering joint disciplinary restrictions on credit, banking, bidding and customs clearance; persistent non-compliance may lead to forced de-registration or revocation of the business license by SAMR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement (annual tax reconciliation return accompanied by audited financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA), local competent tax authority, via the national E-Tax filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to May 31 immediately following the relevant tax year; quarterly provisional returns are due on the 15th day after each quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on any unpaid tax accrues from the June 1 due date; failure to file by May 31 attracts an administrative penalty of RMB 2,000 or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases; underpayment caused by concealment or false statements attracts an evasion penalty of not less than 50% and up to 500% of the underpaid tax; the tax authority may attach, seal and auction assets and will block the WFOE from exit clearance and de-registration until all tax obligations are settled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (annual information report required for all foreign-invested enterprises, including indirect holding structures)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), filed through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System within the integrated one-off annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 in the calendar year following each reporting year; changes in actual control or foreign shareholding must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report or false reporting is recorded as adverse credit publicity; market regulatory and commerce authorities may order correction within a prescribed period and impose joint disciplinary punishment if the enterprise fails to rectify; repeated violations may trigger cancellation of preferential treatment and revocation of foreign-invested enterprise status records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Audit (external Chinese CPA audit of the WFOE statutory annual financial report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the annual Corporate Income Tax final settlement; State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: December 31 fiscal year-end; audited financial statements must be completed and made available for shareholders and statutory filing no later than May 31 for the tax final settlement and June 30 for the SAMR annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of an independent certified CPA audit renders the tax final settlement incomplete and exposes the company to SAMR abnormal-list action; directors and responsible officers may incur personal liability; tax authorities may disregard unaudited accounts, impose assessed adjustments, and penalize the WFOE under the Tax Administration and Accounting Laws.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based safe harbor applies: a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise limited liability company in China is mandatorily required by Article 164 of the PRC Company Law to have its annual financial report audited every fiscal year by an independent Chinese certified public accountant firm licensed by the Ministry of Finance, regardless of balance-sheet size. For quantitative classification and filing purposes: (a) industrial enterprises with annual operating revenue equal to or above RMB 20 million are classified as enterprises above the designated size by the National Bureau of Statistics and are subject to full audited financial disclosure duties; (b) enterprises with total assets above RMB 50 million, annual turnover above RMB 30 million, or employees above 300 are treated as medium or large enterprises and cannot adopt the simplified Small Enterprise Accounting Standards; (c) a WFOE meeting the NBS medium-enterprise threshold of RMB 20 million revenue and 300 employees must include related-party transaction reporting, transfer-pricing documentation and intercompany account verification in the audit scope; (d) even a WFOE using simplified Small Enterprise Accounting Standards remains subject to a mandatory independent CPA audit because foreign-invested enterprise status carries no audit exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Chinese Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS / ASBE / China GAAP), substantially converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); small qualifying enterprises may apply the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards issued by the Ministry of Finance; statutory books, vouchers and financial statements must be maintained in RMB and prepared in Chinese for filing, with English supplementary records permitted where required for group reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not maintain a public UBO register; the WFOE must keep an internal ultimate beneficial owner and actual-controller file in its statutory minute book and must identify the ultimate investor in the annual Foreign Investment Information Report. Any shareholding transfer must be reflected in the Register of Members immediately upon transfer, and the WFOE must apply to SAMR for the change of company registration within 30 days; any change in foreign shareholder or indirect beneficial ownership must also be reported to MOFCOM and SAMR within 30 days. The Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report is the mandatory annual confirmation window for beneficial ownership and shareholding structure.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per annum for a compliant local registered address; USD 1,200 - USD 4,000 per annum for outsourced registered agent and corporate maintenance coordination in major Chinese cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 6,000 per annum for a typical WFOE manufacturing commercial solar inverters; higher fees apply where group intercompany balances, transfer-pricing defense files, or advance pricing arrangements are present

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTEs) under preferential rules; additional 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses (175% total deduction); potential tax holidays for qualifying integrated circuit or software enterprises; Western Development and free trade zone local incentives subject to eligibility, but no general free-zone corporate income tax holiday applies in mainland China.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A02021 Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (EIT annual return) with the electronic filing portal of the State Taxation Administration (e-Tax/自然人电子税务局 and provincial electronic tax bureaus), plus quarterly prepayment form A02015.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with quarterly provisional prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment within 15 days after the end of each quarter; annual EIT reconciliation return within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year (May 31 for a December 31 year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 1 (Enterprise Identification and Basic Information)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, unified social credit code, registered address, tax registration number, industry classification, and enterprise type of the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the PRC WFOE legal name exactly as registered with SAMR; mark enterprise type as 'Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise'; ensure the tax registration number matches the certificate. Cross-border mismatch with the parent's documentation creates a red flag for permanent establishment and beneficial ownership examinations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2 (Covered Accounting Period and Tax Jurisdiction)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates, and whether the taxpayer is filing a full-year or short-period return, including branch combination status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a new WFOE, confirm the first taxable period begins from the date of business license issuance. If the foreign parent treats the WFOE as a tax-transparent entity outside China, reconcile the PRC entity-level EIT treatment to avoid double taxation or mismatched foreign tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue, cost of sales, business taxes and surcharges, selling expenses, administrative expenses, financial expenses, and total profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Book revenue when control and risk pass, and adjust for transfer pricing on intercompany inverter sales to the foreign parent or affiliates. Include export revenue in foreign currency converted at the applicable monthly/periodic average exchange rate; do not net intercompany rebates or marketing support payments unless supported by a written service agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions and deductions: accounting profit, tax adjustments for income not taxable, tax-exempt income, non-deductible expenses, and loss carryforwards. This section produces taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for: (i) unrealized intercompany profits in inventory under transfer pricing; (ii) excessive royalty or interest deductions exceeding arm's length or thin-capitalization debt-equity ratio (2:1 for non-financial enterprises); (iii) non-deductible entertainment expenses (60% deductible capped at 5‰ of revenue) and advertising/ business entertainment caps; (iv) penalty and bribery costs; (v) provisions and impairment losses not yet realized. A WFOE claiming the HNTE 15% rate must record its qualifying core IP and R&D expenditure in the accompanying A107041 form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5 (Tax Credits, Withholding and Prior Payments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, domestic tax credits for qualified equipment, and prepaid quarterly EIT installments already remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE that is a China tax resident may credit foreign income taxes on overseas income, subject to the 'per-country' comprehensive limitation; no credit is allowed for taxes imposed on Chinese-source income. Attach the foreign tax credit schedule. Withholding taxes borne by the WFOE on outbound royalties or interest (if grossed-up by the foreign parent) are generally non-deductible unless statutory requirement exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6 (Tax Payable, Loss Carryforward and Final Settlement)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final EIT payable after applying the headline 25% rate or preferential rate, less prepayments, leading to tax due (or refund).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before submission, complete the annual transfer pricing contemporaneous documentation if the related-party transaction threshold is met; confirm the selected Transfer Pricing method is disclosed in A107012 (related party transactions). For dividend distribution abroad, ensure the board resolution is dated after the EIT return is finalized; profits distributed to a non-resident parent are subject to 10% WHT unless reduced by treaty. A 'deemed profit' transfer pricing adjustment may also trigger late-payment interest and a 50%-500% penalty in a non-compliant low-ball case.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: RMB 2,000 (one-off) plus RMB 20 per day of continued non-compliance after the tax authority's second notice (up to RMB 20,000). Understating tax payable by fraud or false declaration: 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount. Failure to keep accounting books or provision of false documents: RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000. Non-payment after the deadline accrues daily late-payment interest at 0.05% (annualized 18.25%). Criminal tax evasion liability is triggered when unpaid taxes exceed RMB 50,000 and exceed 10% of the tax payable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief on outbound dividends to a non-resident parent, the WFOE must: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the parent's tax authority confirming treaty residence and the financial year covered; (2) obtain the parent's certificate of beneficial ownership (Form 5 or equivalent) proving the parent is not a mere conduit and has economic substance, final control and enjoyment of the dividend; (3) have a shareholding period meeting the applicable treaty requirement (commonly 25% or 10% holding for 12 months, e.g., under China–Singapore or China–Hong Kong DTA as applicable); (4) submit the treaty relief claim through the withholding agent or apply for the 'reduced withholding tax certificate'/preferential rate filing with the Chinese tax authority; (5) maintain contemporaneous evidence of underlying profit source and no-recourse financing or back-to-back arrangements; (6) file the dividend distribution resolution and proof of EIT payment. Where the DTA does not apply, the full 10% PRC WHT is collected at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 10% WHT; treaty-reduced to 5% under many DTA articles where the beneficial owner is the resident of the other Contracting State (e.g., China–Singapore Article 12 often 5% for use of industrial/commercial/scientific equipment and 10% for other royalties; China–Hong Kong DTA Article 12 provides 7% royalty tax rate on certain intellectual property); Interest: statutory 10% WHT; treaty-reduced to 7–10% depending on the DTA, with China–Hong Kong DTA at 7%; excess interest limited by thin capitalization (debt-equity ratio 2:1 for non-financial enterprises) and by general anti-abuse rules requiring arm's length pricing and real commercial purpose.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Yes, the threshold is RMB 200 million or more of aggregate related-party transactions for the year, requiring a contemporaneous Local File and Master File under Announcement 2016 No. 42; additionally, the Annual Related Party Transaction Report Form (A100000) must be filed by May 31, and a Transfer Pricing Special Tax Investigation adjustment risk attaches to transactions exceeding RMB 40 million for a single controlled transaction even below the documentation threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies the substance-over-form doctrine and General Anti-Avoidance Rules under EIT Law Article 47 and Implementation Regulations Article 120, requiring commercial substance and reasonable business purpose for intercompany arrangements. While China is not a member of the OECD Inclusive Framework's mandatory ESR in the same manner as zero-tax jurisdictions, Chinese tax authorities assess Core Income-Generating Activities ('CIGA-equivalent economic substance') for intangible transfers and offshore treasury structures; the WFOE must prove actual personnel, decision-making, risk assumption, and corporate assets supporting solar inverter manufacturing. The value of core functions (manufacturing, risk control over product liability, and quality assurance) must be adequately compensated; a 'cash-box' or 'risk-stripped' WFOE with minimal Chinese substance is subject to recharacterization of profits under OECD BEPS Action 8-10 and SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly under-declaring export revenue on commercial solar inverter sales, fabricating fake purchase invoices or cost invoices, using shell invoices from non-existent suppliers, or causing related-party transactions to be priced at grossly non-arm's length levels to shift profit offshore in the WFOE's annual EIT return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 49 and Tax Collection Administration Law (TAL) Articles 63: a penalty of 50% up to 500% of the underpaid tax is imposed; if the amount evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and accounts for more than 10% of the tax payable, criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201 applies. Late-payment interest at 0.05% per day runs from the unpaid due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for fraud: directors, the financial officer, and the actual controller may be jointly and severally liable for the underpaid tax, interest and penalties where they ordered or actively participated in the act. They face travel bans (exit restriction notices under TAL Article 44), asset freezes and seizure, blacklisting as 'dishonest judgment debtors', confiscation, and up to 7 years' imprisonment in egregious evasion, plus a criminal fine. A person who has been criminally punishable for tax evasion may be barred from serving as a director for a period under the Company Law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance (General Anti-Avoidance and Abuse of Corporate Form)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the WFOE with zero employees, no physical plant or warehouse, no Board of Directors meetings or shareholder resolutions in China, no manufacturing or procurement substance, while the foreign parent invoices the full value-added of solar inverter production to the Chinese entity and uses the WFOE solely to hold the Chinese license and bank accounts, i.e., a conduit or shell used for treaty shopping and artificial profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 47 and Implementation Regulations Article 123: the tax authority may recharacterize the transaction, disregard the WFOE's separate existence for tax purposes where it lacks business substance, and assess tax on the true economic owner. A special tax adjustment may carry a 5-year look-back period and an interest surcharge of 5 percentage points over the benchmark loan rate under Implementation Regulation Article 122. Fines of up to RMB 50,000 may be imposed for false books/records under TAL Article 24/35, and the administrative license or business registration may be revoked under Company Law if the WFOE acts as a shell in violation of public interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the veil when the shareholder uses the WFOE to evade tax or harm a creditor and the corporate form is abused under Company Law Article 20. Directors who signed false resoluti,ans, failed to supervise substance, or allowed asset commingling and severe capital inadequacy are personally liable to make restitution to the tax authority and creditors. A travel ban is routinely issued against the legal representative, and the director may be detained administratively or, if fraud is proven, imprisoned for up to 7 years for tax evasion or up to 3 years for issuing false invoices (Criminal Law Articles 205-206, severely if falsely issuing special VAT invoices).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / False Export & Foreign Exchange Fraud (Money Laundering and Under-Invoicing of Export Receipts)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-invoicing commercial solar inverter exports to foreign related parties and receiving the understated portion through offshore accounts, using third-party shell payees, electronic platform swaps, or crypto converts; misrepresenting the export price in customs declarations and in the foreign exchange monitoring system (SAFE) while falsely claiming foreign income tax credits or obtaining export VAT refunds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Administration Law Article 66 for fraudulent export tax rebates: a penalty of 1 to 5 times the fraudulently obtained refund and criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 204 for those who obtain tax refunds by false declaration; fines of the same magnitude and imprisonment of up to 10 years for serious amounts. False declaration to customs triggers Customs Law penalties and potential forfeiture/confiscation of the invoice value of goods. SAFE may impose a fine of 5%–30% of the foreign exchange amount unlawfully retained/paid under the PRC Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Criminal Law Article 191 (money laundering) and Article 201 (tax evasion), the directors who controlled the invoice manipulation, offshore collection and conversion face criminal liability as principal offenders. The corporate veil is pierced for the dominant shareholder to recover the tax and customs duties plus fines and lose personal assets in execution proceedings. In addition to imprisonment up to 10 years (money laundering) and 7 years (tax evasion), the legal representative will be placed on the exit-restriction/blacklist list, denied credit facilities, and may be prohibited from re-entering foreign C-suite roles in Chinese companies. The company's VAT export rebate qualification can be revoked, and the director's personal bank accounts linked to the unlawful money flows may be investigated and frozen under AML rules.
